text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--The Beirut suburb crisis: Is it a problem of displaced people to be evicted or is it a political campaign? Parliament Speaker Berri warns of strife if evictions are carried out forcibly.
--Prime Minister Hariri met President Chirac again before going to Damascus.
--Foreign Minister Bouez back from Paris. He said Lebanon would not take seriously any Israeli proposals for peace outside the land-for-peace formula.
--Israeli shelling hit a car in the south Lebanon village of Kfar Tibnit and a house in Kfar Roummane.
--Middle East Airlines increased its capital by $47.5 million to $178.75 million.
-The five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon to meet today.
-Hizbollah organized rallies in Beirut and other areas. Secretary General Nasrallah accused President Clinton of justifying Israel's occupation of south Lebanon and the Golan Heights.
--Maronite Patriarch Sfeir says the Pope's visit will give the Lebanese pwople hope for a better future.
